reason: Compact, independent browser PDP-11 emulator implementing kernel/user registers and memory mapping, traps, interrupts, console and RK05 disk I/O, with a disassembler and runnable Unix-oriented HTML frontend.

title: Conway-Macintosh
reason: A native classic 68000 Macintosh Conway Game of Life application written in modern C++ and built using Retro68. Includes cell-field state updates, compact bit matrices, QuickDraw-oriented grid renderers, window/event handling and buttons.

title: FTX X68000 text-plane font library
reason: A native X680x0 text-plane renderer by Yosshin for 8x8 and 16x16 sixteen-color fonts, including sprite-PCG-to-font conversion and palette/scroll operations. The published assembly implementation and C examples preserve a library originating in 1994.

title: PM123 — OS/2 audio player
reason: Native OS/2 Presentation Manager audio player with plugin playback/decoding infrastructure, playlists, audio controls and historical source distribution/build documentation.

title: Unix V4/V5/V6/V7 Resurrection — recovered Unix and browser environment
reason: Source-preservation and browser integration project for Research Unix V4 through V7, combining recovered historical C/PDP-11 source and media with an educational TypeScript frontend, source overlays and a Paul Nankervis PDP-11 bridge.

title: xdfboot
reason: A native X680x0 utility that loads XDF floppy images outside the configured usable memory and patches boot-time ROM access to boot directly from those RAM-resident images. Includes original C image/SRAM control and 68000 ROM-patching code, not an emulator wrapper.

title: Kirby’s Tilt ’n’ Tumble — GBC bank disassembly
reason: Bank-by-bank RGBDS disassembly of the original accelerometer-based GBC title, with native reset/interrupt vectors, header, all 64 assembly banks and checksum manifests.

title: PC98src — onion software original PC-98 sources
reason: Onitama/onion software’s original NEC PC-9801 archive contains historical games, BASIC sources, C utilities, Advanced SOUP compiler and assembly graphics routines. Inspected Crazy World BASIC gameplay, ASC C compiler entry/parser setup and .8086 graphics-bank assembly.

title: osFree Janus Notepad — Wine-derived native Win16 editor
reason: Self-contained native Windows 3.x Notepad adaptation derived from Wine Notepad. C source implements file operations, editor state and Win16 API integration; README explicitly describes removal of Win32-specific dependencies.

title: SEL810 — emulator and paper-tape analysis suite
reason: Kenneth Gober's C# SEL 810 suite includes a substantial processor/memory/console model, TCP peripheral links, tape server, BASIC tape construction, loader-aware tape dumper and control-flow-assisted disassembler.

title: Stars — Amstrad CPC star-field demo
reason: Interactive native CPC star-field demo by Diego Freniche, with separate entity lifecycle, star generation, directional physics and rendering systems; includes keyboard direction and hyperspace effects.

title: TRIPOS — preserved multiarchitecture operating-system sources
reason: Historical TRIPOS BCPL operating-system and tool sources shared with permission from Tim King, covering the shell and utilities plus Nova, PDP-11, LSI4 and Motorola 68000 assembly/compiler support. This is the historical lineage underlying early AmigaDOS, not an AmigaDOS replacement.

title: Cosmo-Engine — Cosmo’s Cosmic Adventure native engine
reason: SDL2 C reimplementation of Cosmo’s Cosmic Adventure with actors, collision, effects, level/container loading, audio and UI. Address-style variables and decoded actor dispatch remain in recovered engine logic.

title: ETH Lilith C18 — adapted Modula-2 multipass compiler sources
reason: Preserved ETH Zürich C18 Modula-2 multipass compiler sources, derived from the 1981 compiler and adapted at Ulm in 1983 for a Lilith emulator under Unix VII. The repository contains actual compiler passes, symbols, code-generation modules, build recipes and steady-state C18 binaries, so it is a source-preservation/toolchain record separate from the emulator that runs it.

title: Vortex II C64 network game
reason: Client/server space-game proof of concept with a native C64 assembly client and Java server. Reviewed vortex.s initializes DHCP/UDP, login, interrupts, sprites and music; server Universe.java creates the shared map, entities, planetoids and destructible scenery.

title: Win3mu — Windows 3 emulator
reason: Open-source release of Topten Software Windows 3.0 emulator. Sharp86 CPU emulation loads Win16 applications while implemented APIs are mapped to modern Windows calls; includes debugging and NE module/heap management.

title: 386SWAT — preserved protected-mode DOS debugger
reason: Original Qualitas 386SWAT protected-mode debugger source archive with extensive assembly, instruction decoding, source-symbol tools, VCPI/DPMI integration and Windows VxD components. Supports debugging native protected-mode and virtual-8086 clients.

title: dosdebug — DOSBox GDB and trace analysis
reason: Reusable Python tools connecting GDB/pygdb to DOSBox guest registers and memory, processing instruction traces, decoding selected DOS system calls and substituting multi-instruction patterns with readable pseudo-operations.

title: Midisurf
reason: Original MIDI rhythm game for Atari ST: one or two players guide dragons to collect notes while the ST sound chip plays selected MIDI tracks. Actual gameplay, MIDI parsing and native GEM graphics are present.

title: MINITS — PDP-11 mini ITS source archive
reason: Preserved Mini ITS executive and device/network software for assorted PDP-11 front ends, terminal concentrators and bridges, with selectable machine configurations and PALX assembly instructions.

title: RSTS/E V10.1 — Y2K and networking maintenance patches
reason: Tony Nicholson’s RSTS/E maintenance repository contains actual BASIC-PLUS FIT date-word fixes, build commands, DECnet/E ONLPAT patches and related PDP-11 utility sources. Scope is maintenance patches, not a complete reconstructed RSTS kernel.

title: XXDP+ monitor — restored PDP-11 diagnostic OS
reason: Ian Hammond’s reconstruction of the XXDP+ HMDLD0 monitor by reverse assembling the XXDP23 binary. A complete monolithic annotated monitor source is preserved alongside binary reference and listings.

title: California Games — BBC Micro conversion
reason: Routine-by-routine reverse-engineering-derived conversion of all six C64 California Games events to a 32K BBC Micro Model B. Native 6502 game rules are adapted directly, with rebuilt BBC graphics, disk overlays and sound; not a game-specific emulation wrapper.

title: Jump N Bump Scorpion port
reason: Scorpion Engine adaptation of the DOS multiplayer rabbit arena game. Contains original-style gameplay scripts for bunny motion, collisions, spring/water/ice behavior, gore, spawning and scoring, plus full maps and assets.

title: Kaboooom! — native OS/2 source continuation
reason: Michael G. Slack’s 1997–1998 Sibyl OS/2 adaptation of Alex Lane’s 1990 minefield-walking puzzle, translated to C/OpenWatcom in 2026. The game implements mine placement, travel/marking and a new bounded safe-cell deduction solver.

title: Moon Knight — Vectrex homebrew
reason: Native vector action game with player/enemy movement, projectiles, frenzy and scoring. MKnight.asm contains the cartridge entry, title/credits states, game state, player/enemy updates and vector/speech data; it is substantial cartridge source rather than a ROM-only archive.

title: MUXX — experimental PDP-11 operating system
reason: Original experimental Mostly Useless eXperimental eXecutive for DEC PDP-11, with C/assembly kernel, process creation and task loading, trap/MMU/clock handling, drivers, shell and sample tasks.

title: ExtFriend — WonderSwan EXT USB firmware
reason: RP2040 firmware turning the WonderSwan EXT port into USB serial and digital stereo audio devices; dual-core TinyUSB service plus UART, PIO and DMA hardware handling.

title: Mutant Fly — recovered BBC BASIC and browser port
reason: Original author’s preservation and direct JavaScript port of FLY, published in The Micro User in July 1985. Includes detokenized/tokenized cassette source, a faithful classic browser presentation and an extended 3D game sharing line-number-annotated rules.

title: Oberon System — LuaJIT and Qt hosted port
reason: Port of the historical Oberon System to an Oberon-to-LuaJIT compiler/runtime and Qt backend, preserving substantial text/viewer/editor/application modules and replacing original inner system services.

title: aap LISP 1.5 — manual-derived C implementation
reason: Independent C reimplementation of LISP 1.5 as described in its manual, with eval and evalquote REPLs, reader, evaluator, cons-cell memory management and library examples. This is neither a mirror nor the IBM 7090 card transcription.

title: ADF tools — native Amiga floppy read/write/copy
reason: Three native Amiga commands read floppy tracks into ADF images, write ADF images to real drives and copy disks with verification, backed by shared track-device I/O code.

title: Bingo/2 — multimedia OS/2 source continuation
reason: E. L. Zapanta’s IBM-era 1992–1994 native 32-bit OS/2 bingo game, preserved with original C and a 2026 Open Watcom build. Source contains randomized card/number creation, multiple bingo-pattern checks, score tracking, printing, virtual hall players and MMPM/2 sound support.

title: CoCo Tools — BASIC translation and image conversion
reason: Expanded maintained Python collection for TRS-80 Color Computer software development. Its substantial DECB-to-BASIC09 translator is beyond the small image-conversion ancestor; retained as one CoCo Tools family record.

title: Cribbage — Sibyl OS/2 card-game source archive
reason: Michael G. Slack’s OS/2 Sibyl/Object Pascal cribbage game source archive, with an engine tracing back through a DOS Turbo Pascal port to David Addison’s Amiga A-basic game. The recovered OS/2 engine scores hands and play, recommends discards and chooses computer cards; visual forms, configuration and resources are included.

title: FrexxEd — programmable Amiga text editor
reason: Daniel Stenberg and Kjell Ericson’s historical Amiga editor sources, continued by Vidar Hokstad, with editing/undo, text folding, scriptable FPL integration, ARexx and syntax-sensitive display.

title: NOAA 940 BASIC — recovered compiler and runtime
reason: Howard Bussey preserves the SDS-940 BASIC implementation he extended at NOAA around 1970 with formatted output, multiple file I/O and strings. Source returned through the Hawaii BCC-500 lineage contains the compiler, runtime and scratch-page sections rather than a modern BASIC clone.

title: BKUNIX — LSX/Mini-Unix restoration and BK port
reason: Leonid Broukhis and Serge Vakulenko's Unix for BK-0010/BK-0011M, derived from revived LSX and Mini-Unix V6 sources. Modernizes ancient C, fixes cross-compilers and relocates the kernel into the BK memory map.

title: The Grenade's Conquest
reason: Native Amstrad CPC two-player arena-action game from SubXplosion’s 2016 academic project. Large C implementation handles characters Jimmy/Obdulia, controls, movement/collisions, ammunition, shots, keys/doors, arena blocks, rounds, score, menus and music.

title: HuDK — PC Engine native development kit
reason: PC Engine ASM/C SDK with native hardware libraries for sprites, video, scrolling, input, interrupts, audio, storage and mathematics, plus desktop graphics/tilemap/VGM tools and runnable source examples.

title: Speeb
reason: Native Amstrad CPC 464 runner by The CiAO Project, written in Z80 assembly with CPCTelera. Separate managers/systems implement scrolling grassfield, levels, player/enemy entities, AI control, physics, collisions, sound, menus, death and victory/restart flow.

title: Murder — native Amiga adventure
reason: Original work-in-progress Sierra-style point-and-click adventure for Amiga. Native C includes room loading, text handling, images, custom screen/UI abstraction and a separate vocabulary/room-data compiler. Distinct title from commercial Murder! and from the author's Parrot project.

title: Stargunner — Neo Geo Pocket Color shooter
reason: Native NGPC scrolling-shooter demo built on NGPC Template 2026. Unlike a bare starter template, it contains a substantial distinct shooter implementation, scripted stages, multiple enemy patterns, bosses, graphics and audio.

title: Paper.io Genesis — native SGDK demake
reason: Authored C/SGDK demake of Paper.io 1 for Genesis, with tile-map territory/path data, human/computer players, movement, claim/fill calculations, score and rendering implemented in src/main.c. Source-level demake rather than game-specific CPU emulation.

title: TOPS-10 ARPANET NCP — Harvard network subsystem source
reason: SAILDART-recovered TOPS-10 ARPANET NCP, IMP driver, FTP and mail subsystem sources. README credits Robert Sundberg for NCP and Edward Taft for FTP/MAIL; actual IMPSER implementation and native FTP link command are preserved.

title: AMOK reverse-engineering maps
reason: Named functions/globals, structure specifications and Ghidra scripts for DOS, Win95 and Saturn builds. This is an analysis corpus, not a completed source port.

title: Ganbare Goemon 3
reason: Work-in-progress Asar reconstruction of v1.0; original ROM required and revisions 1/2 explicitly unsupported. SHA1 comparison target supplied.

title: 3D Pinball: Space Cadet Dreamcast
reason: Dreamcast/KallistiOS port based on k4zmu2a's SpaceCadetPinball decompilation, with documented text-panel rendering issues.

title: AsyncIO Library — classic double-buffered file I/O
reason: Maintenance of the classic39.x asynchronous file-I/O library with double buffering, SDK/startup refactoring and API tests.

title: a314BSD — Amiga sockets through Raspberry Pi
reason: Amiga bsdsocket library proxies requests over A314 to a Pi service, with protocol framing and optional control tools.

title: AXB — Amiga cross-build support
reason: Reusable make definitions and native device/worker examples support vbcc, amiga-gcc, AROS GCC and SAS/C through vamos.

title: BlueSCSI Toolbox — Amiga CD switching and transfers
reason: Native CD Changer and SD Transfer utilities issue toolbox SCSI commands to BlueSCSI V2/ZuluSCSI. Reviewed device capability setup and command dispatch.

title: Opiumxth/amstrad_game
reason: Only a 716-byte source file writes a small fixed drawing then loops forever; the remainder is bundled tools/ROMs. Does not establish the advertised game or a substantive reusable tool. Exclude this snapshot rather than promoting embedded binaries.

title: JumpSTART — Atari ST Personal Pascal launcher
reason: Original GEM launcher supports named program lists, paging, directory handling and window redraw. Source identifies version 2.73a for Geneva and 1991–1993 authorship.

title: MidiMate II — Atari ST MIDI utility archive
reason: Documented historical MIDI utility provides channel/patch control, thru, panic, metronome, channel mapping and monitor modes. Original GFA file, GEM resources and compiled program/accessory are retained.

title: Skweek-inspired browser prototype
reason: The advertised dev branch contains actual PaperScript grid/player/enemy/win-state logic; default branch contains only a pointer to dev.

title: Survivor — browser remake
reason: Substantial browser game and level editor reconstruct the C64 Survivor experience with custom movement/collision/rendering code.

title: Kobuta Rescue — MSX BASIC game
reason: BASIC action game moves floors to rescue pigs while avoiding wolves; substantial state, sprite and input routines are included.

title: dsk2woz — Apple II sector-image converter
reason: Converts standard Apple II sector-image bytes into WOZ track representation and writes CRC metadata. Concrete serializer implementation inspected.

title: Salamander: Operation X — annotated MSX disassembly
reason: 128 KiB SCC MegaROM; banked reconstruction and stage/sound extraction. Primary build recipes and recursive Z80 tracing implementation inspected.

title: Cheer! Christmas Cards — original Forth source
reason: Lloyd Prentice’s original Forth source for 1986/1987 card software, released with permission under MIT.

title: FrankieTheFluff/FluffyFloppy64
reason: The current tree contains only README and FILE_ID.DIZ and announces the project paused/private. Recover a public author release or source snapshot to verify the cataloguing implementation before making a technical record.

title: Apple2Vulcaniser — Vulcan Gold partition preparation
reason: Java utility builds Vulcan partition structures for CompactFlash media, implementing ProDOS block/active-partition constraints.

title: BASICParser — lexical C64 program analysis
reason: Stateful decoder produces text, syntax-tagged token objects and spreadsheet analysis, with PETSCII-aware conventions.

title: PyHunk — Python Amiga object inspection
reason: Standard-library script reports Hunk sections, relocation groups, symbols and debug records.

title: EightBall — native 8-bit language and bytecode VM
reason: High-level language interpreter/compiler emits bytecode for its own VM and includes disassembly tools on multiple 6502 machines.

title: Charcoal — cross-platform text-art tools
reason: CharEdit/CharView handle retro text-art formats and native exports; inspected Atari output implements ANTIC display lists, XEX segments and boot ATR generation.

title: True Love TXB — text-container tooling
reason: TXB unpack/repack scripts manipulate little-endian chunk offsets and compressed text blocks for translation workflows.

title: a2shape — Applesoft shape-table compiler
reason: Packs directional drawing/movement commands into Applesoft shape tables with text or BLOAD-style binary output.

title: x68k — Atari PRG disassembly and 68K translation
reason: C source implements PRG disassembly with code/data/string/table heuristics and 68000 instruction translation to C or i386 output.

title: Apple II Disk Tools — historical catalogue and nibble conversion
reason: Historical a2catalog and a2nibblize implementations generate catalogue/VTOC and nibble encodings, with 13/16-sector variants.

title: extractcas — MSX cassette file extraction
reason: Parses CAS markers and extracts ASCII, BASIC, binary and custom blocks with original addressing metadata.

title: DSKTOOLS — MSX FAT12 image updates
reason: cptodsk writes host files into MSX disk images using FAT12 directory and cluster operations.

title: Slogger Electron Expansion — ROM reconstruction
reason: Partly commented reconstruction of the Electron Expansion 2.02 ROM, including joystick/OS integration and relocated thunks.

title: MSXJuanEditor — constrained tile and sprite composition
reason: Tauri desktop tool edits SCREEN2 tiles/maps and sprite sets, constrains per-row colors and exports JSON, C and raw VRAM data.

title: MSX Sprite Converter — single-color layer separation
reason: Splits 8x8/16x16 images into MSX1 single-color sprite layers and emits assembly or binary in hardware quadrant order.

title: Amiga Icon Converter — Python image export
reason: Converts classic DiskObject icons and IFF-family graphics using palette input, with PNG/ICO/SVG exports and newer icon decoding paths.

title: cambragol/impera
reason: Fork of drcarademono/impera; README clone/release links identify the latter as canonical. Promote the substantive enhanced upstream once, not both copies.

title: nativecode-developer/wings-of-fury-atari-ste
reason: GitHub identifies this as a fork of already tracked theimann/wings-of-fury-atari-ste. Reviewed implementation/backlog but no independent continuation established; avoid duplicating the conversion.

title: MUSICV_2 — portable Wolf Team WM driver recovery
reason: Reimplements original real-mode TSR sequencer, six-channel event handling and OPL3 register generation from WM music data.

title: Darker — native DOS engine reconstruction
reason: Reconstructs Caero/Skimma flight, typed actor state, mission logic, collision and original model rendering in C++ with native-reference checks.

title: Supaplex SPFIX63 — speed-fix disassembly
reason: Annotated assembly/IDA materials reconstruct and explain the previously unpublished Supaplex speed-fix executable.

title: Sierra AGI — recovered logic-script archive
reason: Organizes decompiled Sierra AGI game/demo logic with named variables/controllers and WinAGI project material.

title: brouhaha/apb
reason: Inspected source identifies Apparat PROM Blaster for Apple II and CPU 6502, not PC/MS-DOS software. Outside this explicitly platform-focused pass.

title: ogarvey/DrRiptideDissected
reason: Verified fork of tracked movAX13h/DrRiptideDissected; README retains upstream authors and release links.

title: Operation Europe — native C/C++ reconstruction
reason: Readable recovered game modules with typed supply-budget and state accesses, SDL3 platform layer and original-data loaders, rather than CPU/register runtime.

title: The Need for Speed — recovered physics engine
reason: Hand-rewritten fixed-point tire, drivetrain, collision and traffic physics from DOS/PSX/3DO binaries; inspected formulas retain per-platform address provenance.

title: tape2wav — Spectrum and ZX81 audio rendering
reason: Combines libspectrum TZX rendering and p2raw-derived T81 encoding with coroutine-based sample generation and SDL2 direct playback.

title: OricTapePenKnife — TAP header manipulation
reason: CLI changes BASIC/assembly type and autorun flags, and displays name/load-address information from Oric TAP headers.

title: Solar Realms Elite — C++ BBS-game reconstruction
reason: Terminal game reconstructed from SRE.EXE v0.994b, with structured empire/attack/economy modules and original-compatible data files; emulator comparisons are external tests.

title: ReDMCSB Release 2 — Atari ST Dungeon Master and CSB
reason: Christophe Fontanel reconstruction covers multiple DM/CSB versions with named C, inline 68000 performance routines, boot/load/decompression paths and protection analysis.

title: Test Drive II Enhanced — recovered C engine continuation
reason: Reimplements TD2EGA game core with original data/memory organization and adds modern rendering, launchers and map viewer.

title: mist64/c64ref
reason: A curated reference collection and web presentation of ROM listings/memory maps by multiple historical authors. No distinct new binary reconstruction or original parser is established for this repository; the separately buildable c64rom project is catalogued.

title: lunix — non-promoted Amiga/C64 review
reason: README explicitly calls this an unsupported duplicate of the SourceForge LUnix/LNG repository. Actual C64 kernel, shell/network apps and make-based C64/C128/Atari target sources exist. Find and deduplicate the authoritative LUnix/LNG upstream before counting a new independent project; preserve this URL as a mirror/evidence source. GPL-2.0 repository metadata. Historical README reports partial Atari app-build limitations; not independently compiled.

title: Amiga ASM Development Workflow
reason: Linux automation pipeline for Amiga assembly projects: GIMP/PNG/IFF conversion, ZX0 packing, copper palette/icon generation, assembly/linking and bootable ADF construction. Includes a credited demonstration derived from Bare-Metal Amiga Programming and Salvador decompression; catalogue scope is the integrated development tooling, not a new disassembly.

reason: Fully playable native title port with documented all-world coverage and a bounded demo nondeterminism caveat.

title: a2stuff/a2d
reason: Apple IIGS result is the already tracked Apple II DeskTop disassembly/enhancement project.

title: brunocastello/iWordle
reason: Both declared classic Mac Carbon and OS X builds are PowerPC; Retro68 compiler name alone does not establish 68k support.

title: hleveillegauvin/MacSkate
reason: Author explicitly claims native 68k C game with THINK C 5 on Macintosh Classic. Source and builds are stored only inside nine .dsk files; no direct source listing inspected, so defer until archive extraction.

title: mlaux/gray-brick
reason: Game Boy/Game Boy Color emulator and JIT toolkit targeting 68k Macintosh, not an independently implemented Macintosh game. Its game compatibility list does not create new game records. README explicitly discloses Claude Code assistance, but the tool remains outside this game-only pass.

title: CheungChang7/TI99_HOMEBREW
reason: Aggregate homebrew repository with a generic root description. Review its child title directories and authorship before deciding distinct project scope.

title: Dynamite Dan — ZX Spectrum annotated disassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: SamPuzznic — original SAM Coupé fan conversion
reason: Primary repository documentation and inspected source establish a distinct in-scope retro-development project at the recorded scope.

title: Alex Kidd in Miracle World — byte-matching Master System disassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish game disassembly within tracker scope.

title: BNKCOD — Commodore SuperPET option-ROM disassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish option-ROM disassembly within tracker scope.

title: Commodore LCD KERNAL partial disassembly
reason: Primary repository documentation and implementation establish KERNAL ROM disassembly within tracker scope.

title: Touhou 4: Lotus Land Story — PC-98 source reconstruction
reason: Primary README, current handoff and source establish a maintained 16-bit x86 reconstruction of four original PC-98 products plus a distinct unfinished native x64 port.

title: b2 — BBC Micro-family emulator and debugger
reason: Primary README and implementation evidence establish the independently catalogued scope described by b2 — BBC Micro-family emulator and debugger.

title: kvanderlaag/sg1000
reason: GitHub metadata identifies this as a direct fork of already reviewed barbeque/sg1000; the inspected changes remain within the Soggy-1000 hardware-clone lineage rather than a distinct retro-software project.

title: cpcitor/dsktools
reason: Compared with BackupTheBerlios/dsktools: one added README commit only, no code changes. Promote original source archive once.

title: BBC Lisp — native 6502 interpreter
reason: Interpreted Lisp implementation includes evaluation, reading, printing and mark/sweep GC. README marks tail calls/GC done but notes no string type and inadequate error handling; compilation examples are incomplete.

title: DjPoke/RetroCloner
reason: Modern Lua/LOVE2D visual editor imitates retro aesthetics, but inspected sources do not establish native retro output or a reversing/preservation role. Do not infer native platform support from styling.

title: CiderPress II — Apple II and vintage Macintosh media tools
reason: Archive/disk inspection, extraction and conversion with format-identification and nested-container handling. CLI and Windows GUI have different host support; format recognition is not universal read/write support.

title: bbc-disk — BBC DFS image builder
reason: Builds a DFS SSD image from files with load/execute addresses and optional generated !BOOT. Fixed 80-track, 10-sector, 256-byte geometry is not universal Acorn disk-format support.

title: manatools — Dreamcast audio-bank analysis
reason: MPB/MDB, MLT, OSB and FOB inspection/editing with per-format support. MSB sequences are extractable but not writable; FPB DSP programs remain insufficiently understood.

title: Sonic R Saturn — symbol maps and format research
reason: Publishes named function maps, review records, RNC2 unpacking and screen conversion tools, but no reconstructed C or game executable. Naming all 391 functions does not prove every semantic claim.

title: Sly Cooper — PS2 matching decompilation
reason: WIP engine reconstruction for NTSC-U SCUS_971.98 with separate engine, scripting and data progress. Build accepts extracted assembly/data alongside recovered C++; matching does not mean full semantic recovery.

title: Atari ST development examples — assembly and C
reason: Source examples progress from TOS programs and console input to A-Line graphics. Demonstration collection, not reconstructed commercial games or a full SDK.

title: GameCube File Tools — disc and asset editing GUI
reason: Edits GCM/RARC/BTI/J3D/JPC and compression formats, plus DOL offset inspection. Can create RARC but not new GCM/JPC; BMG scope is currently Wind Waker only.

title: GameCube MusyX tools — sound archive extraction
reason: Source parses MusyX samples, macros and instrument/ADSR structures. Empty root README and template ReadMe.txt do not mean source absent; feature scope is taken conservatively from implementation.

title: Dreamcast reversing diaries — SDK function-ID builder
reason: Guide includes a substantive script generating Ghidra function-ID databases from user SDK libraries. Goes beyond a link list, but is not a game decompilation or shipped SDK database.

title: Dead of the Brain — PC Engine translation research
reason: Print-routine analysis, extraction tools and SQLite script workflow support game1 translation. Repository title includes1&2, but game2 notes are future work.

title: Harvest Moon — SNES annotated disassembly
reason: Banked assembly and memory/script maps from DiztinGUIsh. Code converted to assembly is not fully understood: README marks large semantic gaps and explicitly excludes audio disassembly.

title: Need for Speed High Stakes — PSX matching reconstruction
reason: Matching and reconstruction tracks coexist. Inspected aiinit.c is INCLUDE_ASM wrappers, not recovered C bodies; README percentages are dated author reports, not a current semantic completeness measure.

title: Mega Man Legends — PlayStation decompilation
reason: In-progress US-release decompilation with build/extract scripts. Inspected player.c retains INCLUDE_ASM bodies. README explicitly says code is not yet shiftable.

title: Acorn Format Tools — disk and tape libraries
reason: DFS/ADFS/UEF format readers/writers and conversion utilities. Inspected py2/ADFSlib.py contains little-endian parsing and historical Python2 syntax. A guessed py3path was absent; actualtree path used.

title: VkHandybug — Atari Lynx debugger
reason: Handy-based debugging frontend with conditionalLua breakpoints, memoryspaces andCPUregister access. Inspected editor handles execute/read/write breakpointtypes. Generalplatform debugger, not a bakedgameport.

title: mdgfx — Mega Drive tile tools
reason: CHR conversion and map modification with tile deduplication under flips. Inspected optimizer distinguishes flat/blank tiles and calculates flipped CRCs.

title: AmigaPal — ProTracker sample preparation
reason: Electron/Angular audio preparation for mono 8-bit ProTracker/8SVX output. Current changelog describes JavaScript conversion replacing older SoX dependency.

title: bnGB — Binary Ninja Game Boy plugin
reason: Game Boy loader and architecture plugin. Source validates logo/header and maps the first two ROM banks; do not infer full bank-switch analysis from loader support.

title: giogu75/asm_8048
reason: Primary README and package metadata establish a distinct VS Code language-support tool for Intel 8048 Odyssey2/Videopac assembly.

title: gsgrep — native Apple IIgs text search
reason: Native grep-like utility integrates regex and argument parsing with GS/OS file types, wildcards and recursive search. Implements a bounded regex/option subset rather than complete GNU grep compatibility.

title: ralferoo/cpctools
reason: Collection of lightly modified 2CDT/iDSK sources; unique capabilities beyond the tracked tool lineage and mastering workflow not established. Retain for lineage review, not another independent implementation.

title: gameblabla/videopac-soren-stuff
reason: The mirror preserves attributed historical Videopac/Odyssey source, assemblers and documentation; reviewed KTAA source explicitly targets 8048 and includes a concrete ROM build.

title: CP/M-65 — native CP/M port for 6502-family systems
reason: Coherent native CP/M reimplementation targets many 6502, 65C02 and 65816 machines, provides relocatable applications and development tools, and documents build, release, test and hardware-specific runtime requirements. It does not emulate 8080 binaries.

title: RustyPixelsUK/ManicMinerLL
reason: The listed old owner URL redirects to GitHub repository ID 241390138, matching benbaker76/ManicMinerLL. Preserve as an exact alias of the newly tracked canonical project; no extra project.

title: 64spec c64lib dependency fork
reason: GitHub parent is 64bites/64spec and the README/license retain Michał Taszycki’s original framework. Used by c64lib builds; count the canonical original once, not both roots.

title: Clock Signal — early ZX80/ZX81 repository
reason: Older same-author Clock Signal repository with the same emulator lineage; the current, much broader CLK repository is represented by the promoted Clock Signal record.
